story: Chuck E. Cheese still uses floppy disks in 2023, but not for long
text: WARNING: RANTY STREAM OF CONCIOUSNESS ESSAY AHEAD I just recently started building FOSS in this space in stealthmode, things are not looking good long term. Animatronics as an artform are facing extinction. There are VERY few people in the community with technical expertise to maintain the mechanical and technical aspects of the characters. And companies are abandoning them en masse in favor of screens. To illustrate the HN relevant challenges lets walk through the "stack" of a singing rat. You have the mech itself, its guts a stationary frame made of some material with mechanical extremities attached to it. that are usually animated using either compressed air, or servos. As well as some kind of control board witha bank of relays for actuating said servos/valves. Each character is then connected to a central control box that takes in movements for the entire stage as well as audio or even video to play back in sync. Those movements are all encoded differently just to make this super easy btw :) Lets actually talk about movements next! There are many different companies that produced different shows for Familiy Entertainment Centers and theme parks, all of them programming movements on bespoke systems, as no standard had ever existed. Those movements being stored in a variety of ways. Many of the original Chuck E Cheese and Showbiz Pizza place signals from the late 70s to the early 90s being stored on Reel to Reel tape.
